title: Goulburn and Belmore Park
description: A practical first break from Sydney: picnic gardens, toilets and a playground. The Big Merino is an optional photo stop, rather than a reason to stay overnight.
baby: An easy place for feeding, changing and time out of the car. The Big Merino and Belmore Park are separate stops.
timing: 24 December, on the way to Canberra.

title: Lake Burley Griffin, Commonwealth Park and Carillon
stats: 1–2 hours at your own pace · Free outdoor outing
description: Choose a short section of lakeside path and a picnic. Commonwealth Park and the National Carillon are distinct places along the lake; you do not need to walk the full bridge-to-bridge circuit.
baby: Good for a pram and a flexible outing around naps. Stay beside your baby near the water.
timing: Christmas Day, or an arrival-afternoon stroll.

photos.alt: Lake Burley Griffin and National Carillon

title: National Arboretum and POD Playground
stats: 1–2 hours · Main car park charges apply
description: Sweeping views, planted forests and unusual play structures. Dairy Farmers Hill is a good place to appreciate the setting. The taller climbing pods are primarily an attraction for older children.
baby: Choose short walks and open space. Go early if it is hot; some areas have little shade.
timing: 25 December: grounds and playground open daily under the current schedule. Café, visitor centre and bonsai collection close on Christmas Day.

photos.alt: POD Playground at the National Arboretum

title: Civic and Canberra Centre
description: Explore Garema Place and the pedestrian streets, then pick up groceries. This is a useful city wander rather than a major nature destination.
baby: Easy to shorten if your baby is tired. Canberra Centre provides an indoor break from the heat.
timing: 24 Dec: centre 9am–5pm. 25 Dec: closed. 26 Dec: 8am–6pm. Individual businesses can differ.

title: Braddon and Lonsdale Street
description: The city outing I would prioritise for cafés, small shops and an early meal. Combine with nearby Civic rather than planning a separate half-day.
baby: Choose a relaxed venue with space for the pram. Confirm Christmas Eve service before relying on a particular restaurant.
timing: 24 December after checking in, or the return journey.

title: NewActon and Nishi
description: An optional architecture stop around the distinctive Nishi building and surrounding precinct. Worth a look if you enjoy design.
baby: Short and flexible; outdoor wandering is simplest with the pram.
timing: Add to a city afternoon if time and energy allow.

title: Kingston Foreshore
description: A separate waterfront dining precinct a short drive from Civic. Choose this instead of Braddon when you would prefer dinner beside the water.
baby: The promenade makes an easy outing, with close supervision near the water.
timing: An early dinner on 24 December, subject to restaurant holiday hours.

title: Questacon and Mini Q
description: The indoor choice for Boxing Day. Mini Q is designed for ages 0–6 and offers sensory and exploratory play; the other galleries also give the adults plenty to enjoy.
baby: Baby-change and feeding facilities are available. Prams stay outside Mini Q in the designated parking area. Peak-period Mini Q sessions may be allocated on arrival.
timing: 26 December, around 9am–noon, then lunch and the drive south. Questacon closes Christmas Day. Book general admission ahead.

photos.alt: Current Mini Q mangrove waterplay area

title: National Zoo and Aquarium
description: Choose animals instead of Questacon. This is a substantial outing, so I would not attempt both before driving to Jindabyne.
baby: Use the pram for the longer outing and plan shade and feeding breaks. Optional animal encounters can have separate fees and age restrictions.
timing: 26 December, or on the return journey. Opens 9:30am; closed Christmas Day.

photos.alt: Giraffe at National Zoo and Aquarium
Visitors on a supervised giraffe encounter; encounter conditions apply

title: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve and The Sanctuary
stats: Half-day with driving · About 45 min each way from Canberra
description: The nature alternative to Questacon or the zoo: wetlands, bushland and wildlife. Focus on The Sanctuary rather than the longer summit hikes. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
baby: A better fit for a relaxed family outing than Gibraltar Peak or Camels Hump. Choose your walking distance once there.
timing: 26 December instead of the indoor attraction, or a separate return stop. Closed 25 December. Current vehicle day pass $16.09.

title: Cooma and Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre
description: A useful lunch break between Canberra and Jindabyne, with displays about the Snowy Mountains Scheme. A good option for the adults without committing to another long walk.
baby: Indoor exhibits, toilets and a chance to take a break from the car. Keep any theatre session optional around your baby’s tolerance.
timing: On the southbound or return drive. Published Boxing Day hours 9am–2pm: a morning attraction in Canberra may leave too little time.

photos.alt: Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre in Cooma
Snowy Hydro Discovery Centre Interactive Exhibit

title: Jindabyne and Lake Jindabyne
stats: Base for 4 nights · Flexible lakeside time
description: Stay here for access to both Thredbo and the Perisher/Charlotte Pass side. Use the lake and town for a rest afternoon between mountain outings.
baby: Self-catering, laundry access and a private bathroom are especially useful with your baby. Choose accommodation that confirms space for a cot.
timing: 26–29 December nights in the proposed route. Compare ensuite cabins and small apartments.

photos.alt: Late Afternoon Light on Lake Jindabyne

title: Charlotte Pass and Snow Gums boardwalk
stats: About 400m return · 15–30 min published walking time
description: The best mountain-view stop when you want very little walking. See twisted snow gums and the Main Range from the boardwalk and lookout.
baby: There are steps, and the high location is exposed to wind. A short walk still needs warm layers and stable footing.
timing: 27 December, with Sawpit Creek on the way back. Roughly 45–60 min driving each way from Jindabyne.

photos.alt: Snow Gums boardwalk and mountain views
Snow Gums Boardwalk at Charlotte Pass

title: Sawpit Creek picnic and walking track
description: A woodland and creek walk with a convenient picnic area. An alternative to a full day on the exposed high trails.
baby: Uneven sections mean this is a carrier walk rather than a paved pram stroll. You can simply picnic if the walk does not suit the day.
timing: Combine with Charlotte Pass, or use as the shorter outing on a rest day.

title: Thredbo village and scenic chairlift
stats: Half-day or full day · Lift fees apply
description: A mountain-village day with cafés, scenery and optional lift access to the high walks. The village alone is an alternative if conditions make the alpine walk unsuitable.
baby: Confirm infant and backpack-carrier arrangements directly with the lift operator. Do not assume you can remain wearing the loaded carrier on the chairlift.
timing: 28 December, preferably whichever day has the calmest mountain forecast. Around 35–45 min each way from Jindabyne.

title: Kosciuszko lookout from the chairlift
stats: 4km return · 1–2 hours · Grade 2 for lookout section
description: My first choice for a substantial mountain experience with manageable distance. Elevated walking platforms cross open alpine terrain to views of Kosciuszko.
baby: More exposed than the lower woodland walks. Allow extra time with the carrier and keep the lift’s last return time in mind.
timing: Choose this as the walking part of the Thredbo day, subject to weather and lift arrangements.

title: Rainbow Lake
description: Snow gums, alpine grassland and a quiet lake picnic destination. A gentler choice for your flexible third mountain day.
baby: Gentle climbs and small creek crossings need care with a loaded carrier. Pick a dry day with straightforward crossings.
timing: 29 December, or swap with a higher walk depending on weather.

title: Porcupine Rocks
description: The more substantial shorter hike: snow gums, meadows and granite outcrops with expansive valley views. We Are Explorers highlights this as a memorable introduction to the high country.
baby: Choose it if you have already carried your baby comfortably over similar terrain. Avoid scrambling onto the rocks: there are slippery surfaces and sheer drops.
timing: 29 December instead of Rainbow Lake. Published time excludes baby breaks.

title: Mount Kosciuszko summit
stats: About 13km return from chairlift top · 4–5 hours
description: The iconic summit achievement and a panoramic view from Australia’s highest mountain. The route from Charlotte Pass is longer, about 18.6km return.
baby: A substantial carrier day, rather than an easy family stroll. Build up with shorter outings first, with settled weather and a clear turnaround plan.
timing: An alternative to the lookout walk for a fit, experienced group; not an extra activity on the same day.

photos.alt: Summit Trig Point on Mt. Kosciuszko

title: Dead Horse Gap
description: A scenic combination of alpine views and snow-gum forest. Starting near the chairlift top gives a descending walk to the gap.
baby: Steep sections demand care with a loaded carrier. Arrange pickup at Dead Horse Gap; walking back along the river adds several kilometres.
timing: An alternative Thredbo hike, best for confident walkers. Confirm lift and pickup logistics.

title: Main Range walk
description: The standout full-day landscape walk: glacial lakes, high ridges and mountain panoramas. Starts at Charlotte Pass.
baby: I would not choose this for the easy carrier outing you originally described. It is long and exposed, with a Snowy River stepping-stone crossing that can be impassable.
timing: Keep as an ambitious future option rather than a core part of this family itinerary.

photos.alt: Main Range Walk at Blue Lake

title: Island Bend
description: A Snowy River and bushland setting highlighted in the We Are Explorers mountain road trip. Worth considering for a quiet outdoor break if you are exploring that side of the park.
baby: Treat it as an optional picnic or camping alternative rather than adding another daily drive. Check road and campground status before going.
timing: Optional rest-day alternative to the town/lake. Keep your booked Jindabyne accommodation if you prefer ensuite comfort.

title: Thredbo Diggings
stats: Unpowered campground · Toilets · Bring drinking water
description: A lower-cost camping alternative beside the Thredbo River. Current listing has no camping fee, a $6 booking fee and separate park entry fees.
baby: A basic outdoor stay rather than private-bathroom accommodation. Booking and a suitable site are still required; low camping fees do not remove campervan hire costs.
timing: Compare only if camping itself appeals. Otherwise choose an ensuite cabin in Jindabyne.

title: Berrima, Bowral and Mittagong
stats: One overnight base · Village wandering and meals
description: Choose one town for the overnight stay, then explore nearby waterfalls. Berrima suits a heritage-village stroll; Bowral offers more shops and dining; Mittagong is convenient to the highway.
baby: Avoid moving accommodation between these nearby towns. Compare the total including parking, cot and any minimum stay.
timing: 30 December in the seven-night route, before returning to Sydney on the 31st.

title: Fitzroy Falls
stats: 150m one-way to first lookout · Step-free access
description: The easiest dramatic waterfall stop. Add a portion of the West Rim track if you want more viewpoints and have energy.
baby: The first lookout is the strongest option with the pram or a short carrier outing. Longer rim walks have a different effort level.
timing: 31 December before Sydney. Current vehicle entry fee $4; the visitor centre closes Christmas Day.

photos.alt: Fitzroy Falls viewing platform and gorge

title: Carrington Falls
description: One of the strongest new additions from We Are Explorers: a dramatic waterfall and changing views around the gorge. Combine with nearby Nellies Glen.
baby: The complete loop includes steep metal stairs. Choose the viewpoints that match your footing and energy; short distance does not mean step-free.
timing: Choose this and Nellies Glen as one half-day waterfall outing. Do not try to add every Southern Highlands waterfall in one morning.

title: Nellies Glen
stats: Short walk from its car park · Allow 45–90 min with picnic
description: A small waterfall and shaded waterhole close to Carrington Falls. A change of scale and atmosphere after the big gorge views.
baby: I would make this a picnic and scenery stop with your baby. Wet rock and water edges need close supervision.
timing: Pair with Carrington Falls, rather than visiting on a separate driving day.

title: Belmore Falls
description: A striking waterfall viewed across a forested gorge. A worthwhile alternative if you would like another waterfall after Fitzroy or Carrington.
baby: Stay on the formal lookout route. The track to the base is closed; some final approach roads are unsealed, so check conditions.
timing: An optional substitution in the Southern Highlands, not a requirement to complete the trip.

photos.alt: Belmore Falls in the Southern Highlands

title: Kangaroo Valley and Bendeela
description: A valley-and-river alternative with a chance of seeing wombats at Bendeela. This is farther from the Hume route than staying in Berrima or Mittagong.
baby: Enjoy wildlife at a distance and plan the return drive in daylight. The multi-day kayaking trips featured on We Are Explorers are separate adventures, not part of this baby-carrier itinerary.
timing: Consider if wildlife and valley scenery appeal more than ticking off additional waterfalls. Camping is a separate choice from your preferred ensuite stay.

title: Yarrangobilly caves and thermal pool
stats: Allow a full outing · Northern Kosciuszko detour
description: The most distinctive extension: a forested valley, cave formations and a spring-fed pool at around 27°C. Plan it with Tumut rather than treating it as a quick stop near Thredbo.
baby: The pool walk is steep: 700m each way, Grade 4. The main pool is 2.5m deep, with a separate wading pool. Ask the visitor centre which cave tour, carrier and child-age arrangements suit your baby before booking.
timing: Best with two extra nights around Tumut. The pool has been upgraded; photos can show older facilities.

title: Tumut and the river
description: A riverside town to break the drive and support an unhurried Yarrangobilly day. Choose a motel or ensuite cabin, then continue towards the Southern Highlands and Sydney.
baby: Two nights avoid combining a long mountain transfer, pool visit and another long drive in one day.
timing: Extended route: Tumut nights 30–31 December, Highlands night 1 January, home 2 January. Compare accommodation before choosing the extension.

title: Gibraltar Peak at Tidbinbilla
description: Granite tors and broad views across Tidbinbilla. This is Gibraltar Peak, a different place from the closed Gibraltar Falls.
baby: The summit includes rocky scrambling, so I would choose The Sanctuary instead for your carrier outing.
timing: A more demanding alternative for an experienced group; Tidbinbilla closes Christmas Day.

photos.alt: Granite boulders at Gibraltar Peak summit

title: Camels Hump at Tidbinbilla
stats: A sustained climb with a steep final scramble
description: An ambitious ridge-and-summit outing in Tidbinbilla, mentioned as another mountain-hiking option rather than a recommended easy stop.
baby: The narrow final ascent and scrambling make this a poor match for your original easy-hike request with a baby carrier.
timing: Keep as a future hiking option, rather than adding to the two-night Canberra stop.

title: Blue Waterholes and Clarke Gorge
stats: Remote northern Kosciuszko outing · Unsealed access
description: Blue pools and limestone gorge scenery. The Clarke Gorge walk involves multiple creek crossings; road conditions can affect access.
baby: I would prioritise Yarrangobilly for this family trip. This is a separate adventure, rather than another easy stop on the route to Thredbo.
timing: Consider only with extra time, current road and water-level advice, and appropriate experience. Do not combine automatically with the pool day.
